posts.author: Squareware
caethyril
posts.body:
It fails to render the first screen's worth, but successfully renders henceforth during that play session. That makes me think it's probably a file load issue. Usually a scene waits until its tileset is loaded before starting, but perhaps there's an edge case (ha) somewhere, particularly with browser-based games where loading resources will typically take longer than a local game app.
It may depend on plugins you are using, e.g. tile(set) substitutions, overlays for unexplored rooms, or anything else that affects the tilemap render process.
A potential, generic solution may be to find a plugin to preload all the game's tilesets on game boot. You would want to make sure they are loaded into a persistent, per-session cache; by default MV's image cache implements a pixel size limit (default 10 MPx), clearing older requests to remain at/below that limit.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Good point! More ideas:
Perhaps Edge imposes more restrictions on renderable content, e.g. texture memory. Could also be related to your OS, graphics drivers, hardware configuration, and/or 3rd-party apps.
0:13 is a complete redraw of the black area, minus a bunch of tiles in no obvious pattern. I'm not even sure what triggers the redraw, probably not that deep though.
0:19 looks almost like a bad culling check, like "we stepped over this line, now we need to render these tiles instead". No idea if that's what's happening.
From skimming through
rpg_core
and
pixi-tilemap
, I think the tiles are all sourced from complete tile sheets. And it looks like it just draws autotiles as 4 sub-rects rather than pre-rendering each shape.
If you close the game and try again, does the same thing happen, with the same pattern of tiles?
MV has 2 render modes: WebGL (
ShaderTilemap
) and Canvas (
Tilemap
, a fallback for when WebGL is deemed unavailable). Pressing
F2
during play should show the framerate widget, which will be labelled with the render mode. WebGL may be disabled due to e.g. a (false) negative when checking for WebGL support, user browser settings, outdated graphics drivers, or ancient hardware.
You could try using a plugin like
CommunityBasic
(present by default in new MV projects), to force the rendering mode to
webgl
or
canvas
. If the issue only occurs with one render mode, that could help narrow things down.
Share screenshot(s) of your Plugin Manager, showing all plugins you are using. Game resolution (and the plugin you're using to change it) may also be relevant, since MV only strictly supports 816x624 out of the box.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
No worries! After all, if you experience these things, chances are someone else will too.
That plugin list looks OK. I don't imagine Terrax lighting would affect things like this, and the rest looks pretty innocuous. Probably best to keep YEP_CoreEngine unless you know it's causing a problem...it changes a lot of things, after all. I notice some of the plugins you're using have received updates, but I'm not sure if any of those updates impact this problem.
Opening/closing the menu is a change of scene, so it basically forces everything to re-render. Only 1 scene "exists" at a time: the blurry menu background is actually a snapshot. Does a change of scene also fix the on/off thing from 0:19? Might also be worth testing F4 (toggle full screen) to see if that has a similar effect.
If the game uses Canvas rendering mode (as mentioned, F2 to check) in Edge, you can visit this site ("spinning cube") to see if your browser can use WebGL:
https://get.webgl.org/
If not, double-check you have Edge's hardware acceleration option enabled? The link on that site may provide further suggestions. Otherwise it could be something like Edge failing to properly support a particular piece (or combination) of hardware and/or driver version(s). The HTML specification generally only defines the required outputs, rather than the method used to achieve those outputs.
I wonder if it's something to do with how you've embedded the game on the site, and/or how you're accessing it, e.g. internet vs local network. Both could affect game permissions.
Less reproducibly, it might be related to some kind of data corruption, e.g.
In cookies - you could try clearing cookies for the site;
In RAM/registry - you could try rebooting your system;
In your Edge install - you could try to repair/reinstall it.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
I suspect 88 is a version number, not a year. Windows didn't have a Web browser until the '90s, and it was years before the concept of installing widgets was introduced to browser programs.
You can see in the description of the control that it's permitting (or not) Edge to install widgets, and that didn't exist until Windows 10.
